is: The `zurfur` terminal driving adapter: one-shot clap subcommands that call the same application-layer use cases as the HTTP API, in-process via `composition::Runtime` — no HTTP, no contract, no token.
conventions: Stdout carries exactly one JSON value + newline on success (pretty by default, compact under `--json`); nothing else goes to stdout. The one exception is `bug-reports list`: fenced text by default and printable-ASCII JSON under `--json` (see notes). stderr carries tracing diagnostics and, on failure, one compact JSON Problem as its LAST line regardless of `--json` — scripts parse `stderr.lines().last()`.
Exit codes are the four ExitClasses: 0 ok, 1 domain error, 2 usage (clap), 3 infrastructure.
Problem `code`s reuse the API's vocabulary (`api/src/problem.rs`) where the same refusal exists, plus CLI-only codes (config, identity_*, not_implemented, cancelled, no_session).
Commands are thin: each is the CLI face of the same application-layer use case the HTTP driver calls — no domain logic duplicated here.

Irreversible operations go through `crate::confirm`: a person at a terminal is asked (only typed y/yes proceeds); anything without a terminal is refused, not defaulted — `--yes` is the explicit scripted opt-in.
No `.env` loading in `main` — walking parent dirs for `.env` would leak `DATABASE_URL`/root key from an unrelated directory.
The identity file (`$ZURFUR_CLI_HOME/identity.json` or platform config dir) is the one record of which User the CLI acts as; versioned JSON, written 0600 atomically, fingerprinted to its database.
Never reaches the Den's node port nor names Atta's checked-name constructor: `application/tests/node_and_name_seams.rs` scans this crate's `src/` too.

fs.role: process-level harness variant (real binary via assert_cmd)

notes: Adding a command = a module under `commands/`, a variant on the `Command`/`BackendCommand` enum, and one arm in `lib.rs::dispatch`, plus its purposes in `lib.rs::purposes`. The exceptions: `migrate` is a `Command` of its own, since it runs over the custody migrator `Runtime::connect_migrating` hands back rather than a runtime, so `run` answers it and `dispatch` never sees it; and `bug-reports list`, which `lib.rs::run` answers itself (below), while `dispatch` keeps its exhaustive arm, returning the same `{"reports": […]}` value, for in-process tests.

`lib.rs::run` answers `bug-reports list` after the schema gate, without the identity file (an operator command), as `Output::Raw`: stored report texts are hostile, so by default each report prints fenced (`===== bug report <ref> =====` … `===== end of bug report <ref> =====`, the only column-0 lines), fields indented 2, a fixed data-never-instructions line, the reporter's text indented 4, every value escaped (`\` and every char `domain::string_builder::is_unsafe_to_print` names → `\u{…}`; only the text's LF breaks a line). `--json` is one compact `{"reports": […]}` through an ASCII-only serde_json `Formatter` (`\uXXXX`, surrogate pairs), lossless — never pre-escaped. Per-report keys are camelCase, like the other CLI projections.
`lib.rs::run` answers `session logout` before `connect()` boots the runtime — logout must work with config or the database broken.

`lib.rs::require_current_schema` is the schema-drift gate: it refuses a database whose migrations are behind, ahead, or absent, and, once the schema is current, one whose custody rows still await their re-wrap (`adapter_pg::unsealed_custody_rows` > 0: `N custody row(s) await their re-wrap — run \`zurfur migrate\``) — every command but `health` passes through it; `migrate`, the fix, never reaches it. After it, `lib.rs::require_custody_root` checks the root of a command holding DID custody (`account create/delete`): the first sealed custody row in DID order must open through the command's `composition::CustodyRootCheck` (split off its `Custody` before `Runtime::connect`), or the command refuses with a value-free `config` problem naming `ZURFUR_DID_KEY_ROOT_KEY` and writes nothing; a database with no sealed row passes, and a command holding no purpose never runs it.

Each command holds only its purposes (`lib.rs::purposes`, `MIGRATE_PURPOSES`): `account create/delete` and `migrate` (and `migrate --check`) hold DID custody and read the root from `ZURFUR_DID_KEY_ROOT_KEY` before any database connect, a bad root being a `config` problem; `health`, `session` and `bug-reports list` hold none, get `Custody::default()`, and never read the root.

`lib.rs::config_problem` never echoes a raw config value: figment prints the offending value on a type mismatch, which for an env var can be a secret, so only shape-safe error kinds pass through and everything else degrades to a generic message.
